Do I have the audience, systems, or capacity to support it?
How will I know if it was successful?

The BEST investment decisions aren’t emotional. They’re intentional.

caption:
We are big fans of AI over here. It’s changing the game for so many small business owners! 🙌

You can now automate admin, streamline payroll, speed up calculations that used to take hours - the efficiency alone is worth it. And when you know your numbers well, AI helps you move faster and think bigger. We love that for you.

But there’s one thing we want you to keep in mind as you use it for your finances: AI is only as good as the prompt you give it, and the prompt is only as good as the person writing it.

We had a client come to us recently with an AI-generated set of projections that had them growing from $250K to $1.2M in six months. Exciting, right? Except there was no roadmap, no plan, no checkpoints. AI built exactly what it was asked to build, it just didn’t know enough about the business to push back or fill in the gaps.

We don’t think that’s a reason to stop using it, but it is a reason to use it smarter.

Ask better questions going in. Vet what comes back. And for the big strategic stuff, use AI as a starting point, then bring it to your accountant (that’s us!) to pressure test it.

caption:
International Women’s Day is a celebration, but it’s also an opportunity to challenge something.

After 17+ years working with entrepreneurs, here’s what I see:

Women are capable of building incredibly profitable businesses.

But many of us were conditioned to prioritize impact over income. Service over sustainability. Everyone else over ourselves.

We celebrate men for building to exit. We question women for wanting the same.

And that subtle difference shapes how we build.

This is NOT about choosing money over heart. At the end of the day, it’s about understanding that profit is what allows you to:

💵 Pay yourself properly
💵 Support your family
💵 Hire well
💵 Deliver better
💵 Give generously
💵 Stay in business

I’ve built it both ways.

The version where profit was an afterthought (it was exhausting), AND the version where profit became a priority and created stability, freedom, and MORE impact.

Today, ask yourself: Do I truly believe it’s okay to want to make money in my business?

Then ask another woman what she wants to earn this year.

Let’s normalize women making money. Out loud.

I think we all know by now that pricing services isn’t as simple as pulling a number out of thin air. It’s time to face the facts: your prices need to cover more than just your client-facing hours.

Start with the basics: How much do you want to make? Divide that by the hours you’re actually spending working with clients. That’s your starting point. But don’t stop there. As your business grows and you start layering in things like rent, team wages, or overhead, the math gets a little more complex. And that’s okay!

If you’re managing a team, you have to factor in their wages and your own time spent overseeing their work. You’re not just charging for client hours anymore; you’re charging for the behind-the-scenes time that keeps the business running.

Look at your full list of expenses for the month. What can’t be tied directly to a client? What’s your team getting paid? How much time are you really putting into the work? You need to have a clear understanding of ALL of that before setting your prices.

Don’t be afraid to ask for help with the math, there are industry standards out there that can guide you, but ultimately, YOU have to know YOUR numbers. Get clear on your costs and value, and price accordingly. No more guessing or undercharging. Know your worth, then make it work for you.

I wouldn’t have it any other way. Being on the other side, every high and low was worth it.

caption:
In this episode of Small Business School, I sit down with Kelly Lorenzen @duplicatemyselfklm, CEO of KLM Consulting. With over 22 years of business ownership experience, Kelly shares her insights on scaling a small business by focusing on what you love and outsourcing the rest. From building the right team to embracing technology, Kelly’s advice is packed with actionable steps for busy entrepreneurs.

Key topics covered:

✨Outsource Smartly: Identify tasks that are repetitive and low-expertise. Document these processes through video tutorials to make delegating easier.

✨Focus on Your Zone of Genius: Do what you love most in your business and hire experts for bookkeeping, marketing, and administrative work.

✨Embrace Being the Face of Your Business: While you can outsource many marketing tasks, showing up personally on video, social media, and podcasts is key to building trust.

✨Build a Team the Right Way: Start by creating a detailed task list, separate what requires your expertise, and delegate the rest. Hire intentionally and train effectively with SOPs.

✨Embrace Technology: Don’t fear software. Implementing the right CRM and automated systems can drastically reduce manual work and improve efficiency.

Tune in for practical tips that will help you scale your business faster — and with less stress!

caption:
Looking at your finances isn’t about obsessively checking your bank balance, it’s about knowing your numbers well enough to make confident, informed decisions.⁠
⁠
With my best clients, they don’t need to know every single cent that’s coming and going, but they know enough to feel comfortable deciding whether to put more energy into a project, scale their efforts, or shift priorities.⁠
⁠
Understanding your financial landscape doesn’t require you to be a mathematician, it just means having a sense of your range so you can take strategic actions.⁠
⁠
If you’re not tracking your numbers or feel unsure about your finances, now is the perfect time to start! 🙌⁠
⁠
How do you stay on top of your numbers in your business? Drop your tips for this community in the comments!⁠
